lyrics:
[Intro: clean eerie guitar figure, toms build, distorted riff arrives]

[Verse 1: gruff, barked, heavy palm-muted riff]
Lock the door and check it twice
Leave the phone to charge its light
Close your eyes, it's getting late
Every worry learns to wait

[Pre-Chorus: half-time, menacing]
Keep the blanket to your chin
Don't ask what the dark lets in

[Chorus: huge, gang shout on the first words]
Lights out
Count the wolves
One for the money, two for the years
Three for the things you can't undo
Lights out
They're counting you

[Verse 2: gruff, barked, riff heavier]
Something's ticking in the pipes
Something's due you didn't write
Three a.m. is at the door
It's been here many times before

[Pre-Chorus: half-time, menacing]
Keep the blanket to your chin
Don't ask what the dark lets in

[Chorus: huge, gang shout on the first words]
Lights out
Count the wolves
One for the money, two for the years
Three for the things you can't undo
Lights out
They're counting you

[Guitar Solo: wah pedal, fast, wailing]

[Spoken: clean guitar only, tired man whispers, a child answers]
One: did I lock it?
(Go to sleep, Dad)
Two: did I say it?
(Go to sleep, Dad)
Three: will they be alright?
(We're alright. Go to sleep.)

[Bridge: riff returns, building, sung low]
Hush now, grown-up, close your eyes
Morning always tells the night it lies

[Final Chorus: heaviest, double-time drums at the end]
Lights out
Count the wolves
One for the money, two for the years
Three for the things you can't undo
Lights out
They're counting you

[Outro: riff strips back layer by layer to the clean guitar, fade]
Lights out
Lights out
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 123 BPM, 4/4, E minor. A heavy, mid-tempo stomp with a swing in the riff. Menacing and controlled.

VOICE: Male baritone, gruff and percussive, barking the ends of lines with a growl. Low and almost crooned in the bridge. A whispered adult voice and a clear, calm child's voice in the spoken section. Gang shouts on the first two words of each chorus.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar playing a slow, uneasy figure. Layers of tightly palm-muted, heavily distorted rhythm guitars. Deep, clanking bass locked to the kick. A powerful drum kit with a dry, cracking snare and booming toms. A lead guitar with a wah pedal for the solo. No keyboards.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, clean guitar alone, toms and bass join, the distortion fades in and the full riff lands at 0:38. 0:55 Verse 1. 1:14 Pre-chorus in half time. 1:24 Chorus 1. 1:47 Verse 2. 2:06 Pre-chorus. 2:16 Chorus 2. 2:39 Guitar solo with wah. 3:02 Spoken section over the clean guitar. 3:22 Bridge, the riff returns under two sung lines. 3:34 Final chorus. 3:57 Outro, the layers peel away in reverse until the clean guitar is alone, fading by 4:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-90s big-budget metal: thick, dry and very wide, guitars quadruple-tracked, the kick and snare up front, vocals doubled.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The spoken count at 3:02 and the child's voice answering.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The roles are reversed. The fears are an adult's list and it is the child who says everything is fine. That makes the heaviest song in the pack one of the gentlest.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Dread, menace, then reassurance from an unexpected direction.

WHAT IT IS ABOUT

The monster under the bed grew up with us. Now it is the three o'clock list of worries, and the one lying awake is the parent.

THE OTHER WAYS TO HEAR IT

Hear it as: adult insomnia; a child's nightmare, exactly as before; debt; a soldier's night watch; or a menacing entrance theme. In the spoken section the child comforts the adult.

ENGINEERED HOOKS AND THE DESIGNED MISHEARING

Borrowed mechanics: comfort turned to threat, a clean riff that builds by layers, a two-syllable chorus shout, and a spoken call-and-response with a child. Designed mishearing: 'count the wolves' is heard as 'count the walls', which is what the sleepless do.
